notes: A0 is a bounded FIFO/polling approximation, not an unmodified production performance measurement. A/B share eligibility, provider limits, global capacity and fair admission.
Replay scales service times and intervals 20x; SQLite and instrumentation overhead remain real. This is not a live speedup prediction.
Original eight scenarios ran together; quarter-second scenario was a subsequent separate process. Three shuffled-order repeats per scenario; no statistical significance claim.

First 72 trials loaded source before addition of dead-worker error reporting; successful dispatch paths unchanged. Supplemental nine trials include it. Database-failure regression tests cover the final source.

First-result times are observed persisted progress after polling, not network or UI latency. Per-provider dispatch delay is relative to the provider-only eligibility lower bound and includes global-capacity/fairness/admission waiting.

RSS is per-process lifetime high water on macOS; not independent per-trial allocation. SQL timing is statement execution, not complete transaction/claim time. CPU sampling excludes initial job admission while elapsed includes admission.
Trace times are seconds since trial admission; labels and responses are entirely synthetic. Throughput counts physical provider calls; successful items include shared followers.
A/B fair ordering uses durable millisecond timestamps and separately ranks direct/shared work. Unified mixed-class fairness and exact durable ordering remain implementation gates.

Zero-interval fast tests are offline stress controls, never proposed live provider intervals. Physical-slot extension in the prototype is single-owner accounting, not a multi-process execution guarantee.
